title: Deadlock in money transfers
root_cause: transfer() locked rows in argument order: sender first then receiver (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on from_id, then to_id). Two concurrent opposite-direction transfers between the same pair (A->B and B->A) each hold one row lock and block forever on the other, forming a lock-ordering cycle that PostgreSQL aborts with 'deadlock detected'. The deadlock reports confirm both sides wait on the same SELECT ... FOR UPDATE statement.
fix: Acquire both row locks in a globally consistent ascending account-id order (lower id first) regardless of transfer direction, handling the self-transfer (from_id==to_id) case with a single lock. The funds check still uses the sender's locked balance and updates are unchanged, so sequential behaviour is identical. Disjoint account pairs lock disjoint rows, so unrelated transfers still run fully in parallel (no table/global locks, no SERIALIZABLE/NOWAIT retries needed).
